title: How student protesters won against Serbia's Vučić
description:
Snap elections in Serbia have resulted in the toppling of the long-term leader, Aleksandar Vučić, as protest movement ‘The Student List’ won a decisive victory over the weekend. Over the last two years, students have protested against the government after a concrete roof collapsed outside of a train station and 16 people were killed. Lots of people saw the disaster as a result of corruption and negligence in the country. We hear from people on the streets of Belgrade celebrating this new era. But how did this win come about? Who will lead the country? And what is next for Serbia?

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討塞爾維亞學生運動如何在提前大選中擊敗長期執政的領導人 Aleksandar Vučić 與其陣營。這場抗爭始於 2024 年火車站混凝土雨棚坍塌造成 16 人死亡的事故，大眾認為這是政府貪腐與疏失所致。在創紀錄的高投票率下，由學生支持且涵蓋各領域專家的候選人陣營獲得 52.6% 的選票，擊敗得票率 39.2% 的 SNS 執政黨。該陣營提出打擊貪腐與改善民生等 11 項方案，並採用無單一領袖的分權合作模式。隨著年底前需舉行總統大選，此結果為塞爾維亞帶來新氣象。
summaryEn: This episode explores how a student-led protest movement in Serbia achieved a decisive victory over long-term leader Aleksandar Vučić in recent snap elections. The protests began two years ago after a renovated train station's concrete canopy collapsed, killing 16 people—a disaster widely blamed on government corruption and negligence. Supported by a coalition of professionals without prior political experience, the student-backed list won 52.6% of the vote compared to 39.2% for Vučić’s ruling SNS party. The movement advocates for anti-corruption reforms, media transparency, and social welfare through a decentralized leadership structure. With a presidential election required before the end of the year, this victory marks a historic moment for Serbia and offers inspiration to student movements globally.
